title: introduce-threshold-oracle-and-deferred-throttle-gates-for-dedicated-fleets
author: Avery Chen
description: Context: Dedicated fleets need finer-grained admission controls to preserve tenant throughput guarantees during transient spikes without wasting reserved capacity. Motivation: existing backpressure and burst-token systems react after congestion has already impacted latency/SLOs; we want a conservative, forward-looking gate that prevents risky admissions when headroom is predicted to be insufficient. What this PR implements: a lightweight "threshold oracle" that synthesizes short-term utilization forecasts (EWMA + percentile sampler) and a risk sigma coefficient to produce a per-tenant safe-admission threshold, plus a deferred-throttle gate that pauses burst admissions for a configurable window when predicted risk crosses the configured threshold. The implementation is conservative by default and opt-in per fleet/tenant (config flag is off for existing fleets). Key behaviors: 1) Oracle computes a 30s and 5m smoothed utilization window, combines them with a tunable sigma multiplier and a percentile-of-samples safety margin to produce a numeric "admission headroom" score. 2) Deferred-throttle gate integrates with the existing admission pipeline (AdmissionController -> BurstTokenPool) and can defer acceptance of burst tokens for a tenant for a configurable cooldown when the oracle signals elevated risk. 3) Telemetry: emits new metrics (tenant_admission_headroom, tenant_risk_sigma, deferred_throttle_events) with tags for tenant_id, fleet_id, and policy_version. 4) Rollout: feature gated, default disabled; can be enabled per-fleet in dedicated config; operator can choose conservative defaults used in initial rollout. Design notes: - Oracle is intentionally local and stateless (uses sliding-window counters and percentile sampler) to avoid cross-fleet coupling and to make rollout lower-risk. - The gate uses exponential backoff for repeated deferrals to avoid oscillation and includes an override annotation for emergencies. - We preserve existing burst-token accounting (no change to token economics) but reduce accidental admissions when predicted headroom is insufficient. Migration: no required DB migrations. Config knobs added for fleet config proto (threshold_oracle.enabled, threshold_oracle.sigma, threshold_oracle.window_seconds, deferred_throttle.cooldown_seconds). Testing: unit tests for oracle math and gate, e2e in perf-canary harness with synthetic tenant spike. See related Linear items ENG-3241, ENG-3308.
commits: a1f4d89: add threshold oracle core + percentile sampler
d3b7e10: wire oracle into admission controller and add deferred throttle gate
f6c0123: expose config knobs and fleet-level opt-in
c9be2a7: add telemetry metrics and prometheus scrape labels
b48f9d2: unit tests and perf-canary e2e scenario
ff34a00: docs/observability: document new metrics and alert recommendations
review_comments: Jordan Rivera: Nice isolation between oracle and gate. Question: why percentile sampler instead of full histogram? Response: sampler reduces memory pressure for large tenant counts and gives sufficient tail signal for admission decisions.

Sana Malik: Can we expose a diagnostic export for the oracle's internal state? Reply: added a debug endpoint behind admin auth that returns last N samples and EWMA state (see telemetry/metrics.yaml change).
Omar Ibrahim: Concerned about oscillation with backoff windows. Reply: the gate now uses exponential backoff with jitter and a min-cooldown floor; added tests simulating repeated spikes.
testing: unit: oracle math edge cases and sampler correctness (pkg/autoscaler/oracle_test.go)
integration: admission path with oracle enabled against local BurstTokenPool simulator
perf-canary: synthetic tenant spike scenario run in staging (cmd/perf-canary/scenarios/threshold-oracle.yaml) showing 42% fewer SLO breaches under default conservative config
rollout_plan: step 0: keep feature disabled in global defaults
step 1: enable for non-critical fleets in staging for 7 days; monitor tenant_admission_headroom and deferred_throttle_events
step 2: enable for a small set of production fleets (opt-in) with sigma=2.5 conservative setting
step 3: evaluate telemetry for 2 weeks; consider lowering sigma or adjusting windows per workload
release_notes: Added Threshold Oracle and Deferred Throttle Gate for dedicated fleets (opt-in).
No changes to burst-token accounting; default behavior unchanged until enabled per-fleet.
